About Base

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role

At Base, we’re building the future of residential energy. Our unique battery, power inverter, and interconnection systems are designed from the ground up to deliver affordable, reliable, and resilient power to households that are underserved by today’s aging and overloaded electrical grid.

Unlike conventional energy storage solutions that cost 5–10x more, our vertically integrated approach allows us to deliver larger, more powerful batteries at a fraction of the price. We’re combining innovative hardware, clever business models, and local manufacturing to get this product in the hands of real people–fast.

As a Hardware Engineering Intern, you'll be hands-on with every phase of product development–from early prototyping to production support. You'll work alongside experienced engineers in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment, solving challenging problems in mechanical and electrical design for cutting-edge batteries, inverters, and microgrid interconnection devices. You’ll learn by doing–and what you do will ship.

What You'll Do

- Collaborate with senior engineers to design, simulate, build, and test electrical and mechanical systems.

- Participate in hands-on prototyping, debugging, and iterative testing of early- and late-stage hardware.

- Support both R&D and production efforts–from first breadboard to high-volume manufacturing.

- Help diagnose and solve real-world performance, thermal, and integration issues.

- Contribute to system documentation, test procedures, and design reviews.

What You'll Bring

- Current junior or senior in an undergraduate program, or a graduate student, in Engineering, Physics, Math, or a related technical field.

- Strong understanding of electrical or mechanical engineering fundamentals (depending on focus).

- Passion for hands-on hardware development and building things that work in the real world.

- Electrical focus: familiarity with schematic capture and PCB layout tools (e.g., KiCad, Altium) is a plus.

- Curious, self-motivated, and eager to work on hard problems with real-world impact.

Why Base?

You won’t be stuck on the sidelines. At Base, interns contribute to meaningful product work that ships. You’ll gain real experience with real stakes–mentored by engineers who’ve built systems at scale across the energy, aerospace, and hardware industries. This is a chance to make a dent in the energy transition, not just study it. Come help us build something better.

Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.

Our Values

- First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

- Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

- Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

- Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

- Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

- Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

- Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.

Do the best work of your life at Base.

Overview

Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.

Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.

About the Program

Keysight's AI team builds adaptive engineering intelligence systems where measurement, simulation, and machine learning converge - models that learn from complex physical data and adapt to new design and testing conditions.

This internship focuses on machine learning surrogate models for engineering simulation and measurement. High-fidelity simulations and physical measurements can dominate the design and test loop for RF, high-speed, and other engineering problems, and their cost limits how much of a design space an engineer can explore. You will develop models that predict engineering responses at a fraction of the cost, investigate how such models can be adapted efficiently as the design problem changes, and integrate the result into an engineering ML runtime environment.

Role Overview

You will design, train, and evaluate neural surrogate models that predict engineering responses from simulation or measurement data far faster than repeated high-fidelity simulation or physical characterization. This spans the full arc of the problem: generating or assembling the data, choosing and evaluating model architectures and output representations, establishing where accuracy holds and where it degrades, and quantifying the result against a realistic simulation or measurement budget.

In the second phase you will study how a trained model can be specialized efficiently when the design problem shifts, using LoRA and related parameter-efficient adaptation methods. You will work alongside AI researchers, simulation and measurement experts, RF designers, and runtime engineers.

Learning Outcomes

- Apply modern machine learning to realistic engineering simulation and measurement data.
- Learn how surrogate model accuracy depends on data quality, sampling strategy, representation choices, and simulation budget.
- Develop practical experience with parameter-efficient adaptation methods such as LoRA under data-scarce engineering conditions.
- Build fluency with uncertainty estimation, physical consistency checks, and engineering-relevant error analysis.
- Take a research model from Python experimentation toward robust C++ and LibTorch integration.
- Collaborate across machine learning, RF design, simulation, measurement, and runtime engineering disciplines.

Responsibilities

- Generate parametric engineering datasets using simulation and/or measurement sources, with attention to sampling strategy and to numerical noise in the underlying data.
- Design, train, and evaluate neural surrogate models for engineering response prediction.
- Investigate how the choice of output representation affects accuracy, particularly across operating regions or frequency ranges where the response varies sharply.
- Establish rigorous baselines and quantify accuracy as a function of simulation or measurement budget.
- Evaluate LoRA and related parameter-efficient methods for specializing trained models to new problem settings, against full and partial fine-tuning.
- Develop calibrated uncertainty estimates so that predictions can be trusted or deferred appropriately.
- Verify physical consistency and engineering constraints - including passivity, causality, and reciprocity where applicable - and report engineering-relevant metrics including worst-case behavior.
- Analyze the simulation corpus and model behavior: parameter sensitivity, response dimensionality, data quality and solver noise, and where prediction error concentrates across frequency and design space.
- Prototype model training and inference integration in C++ and LibTorch within an engineering ML runtime environment.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Electrical or Electronic Engineering, or a related technical field.
- Hands-on experience across multiple neural architectures - transformers, neural operators, graph networks, CNNs - and sound judgment about which suits a given problem.
- Strong Python and PyTorch, with experience training and debugging neural networks well beyond tutorial scale.
- Strong C++ and hands-on LibTorch experience to implement and integrate models into a production runtime.
- Solid grasp of transfer learning, fine-tuning, and parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA.
- Strong applied statistics and exploratory data analysis, including sensitivity analysis and dimensionality reduction, and the judgment to diagnose a model from its errors rather than its aggregate score.
- Experimental discipline: rigorous baselines, careful ablations, experiment tracking, reproducible results.
- Willingness to learn the underlying physics rather than treat it as arbitrary numerical data. Mentorship will be provided.

Preferred Qualifications

- Background in RF, microwave, high-speed digital, or test and measurement engineering; familiarity with S-parameters, filters, or interconnect.
- Experience with EM simulation tools and their scripting interfaces, such as Keysight ADS, RFPro, Momentum, or comparable tools, or engineering measurement and test automation environments.
- Experience with surrogate modeling, operator learning, physics-informed machine learning, or scientific machine learning generally.
- Experience with uncertainty quantification, conformal prediction, or Gaussian process regression.
- CUDA, cuDNN, or TensorRT experience, or prior experience shipping a research model in C++.

Prerequisites

- Version control, modular code structure, and reproducible experiment pipelines.
- CMake and Git workflows for sizeable C++ projects, and comfort profiling and debugging C++ code.
- Ability to design an evaluation that answers a question rather than one that produces a favorable number.
- Clear technical communication to both machine learning researchers and engineering stakeholders.

What This Internship Offers

- Apply modern machine learning to physical engineering data in an industrial setting.
- Learn parameter-efficient adaptation and transfer learning under severe data scarcity.
- Develop working fluency in RF and high-speed concepts, measurement data, and simulation workflows.
- Take a research model the full distance, from Python prototype to robust C++.
- The opportunity to shape how machine learning accelerates engineering design and test at a company that builds both the simulators and the instruments that validate them.
- Mentorship across machine learning, simulation, measurement, and RF design, with access to engineering tools and realistic engineering datasets.
- A portfolio-defining project spanning scientific machine learning, efficient model adaptation, and real-world engineering applications.

Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. KLA's Central Engineering organization is made up of nine Centers of Excellence (CoEs) spanning disciplines like automation, motion control, sensors, platform design, and packaging. Each CoE contributes not only technical deliverables but also deep expertise, best practices, and advanced tools that elevate both what we build—and how we build it.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.

In this role:

- Work with traditional and deep learning algorithm techniques, such as optical, physical, and mathematical modeling, inverse problems, and AI models to meet and improve results on KLA products.
- Experiment with new and novel techniques to improve results or reduce compute cost of various modeling techniques for processing and analyzing measurement spectra and images.
- Build signal/image processing and analysis tools for more efficient experimentation.
- Manage measurement and imaging data used for training and experimentation of AI and physics modeling systems.
- Develop software tools and solutions processing and analyzing measurements and images for KLA products.
